Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back folks for India's response and chase with the bat. The umpires and players are out to the middle. Australian players scatter out to the field. India has opted for a light roller as Rohit Sharma and Yashasvi Jaiswal walk out to the crease. It will be Mitchell Starc to get things underway with the new ball. Three slips and a gully waiting. Off we go...
... FOURTH INNINGS ...

Right then, after a back-breaking work with the ball from India, 340 runs separate the two teams with the momentum surely tilted in favor of the hosts. And given the way the Indian batting order has struggled to form partnerships, it is a huge, huge ask, coupled with the pitch which has shown signs of a bit of deterioration now. It is not going to be an easy task for the tourists at all. A minimum of 92 overs remain, Australia need 10 good deliveries to win and take an unassailable lead in the series. The chase on the other side. Do not go anywhere.

Siraj returned to claim the prized wicket of Labuschagne. However, by this point, Pat Cummins had grown comfortable at the crease and took command of the innings. The Australian captain showcased his batting prowess by crafting a valuable 41 runs while expertly managing the tail-end batters, before eventually falling. It was then Lyon and Boland's last-wicket stand that troubled the Indian bowlers for exactly 20 overs and added more runs to the total before Bumrah eventually got the job done early in the day and finished with a spectacular 5-fer and also completed 200 Test wickets.

Labuschagne, who notched a 72 in the first inning, remained absolutely unfazed despite wickets tumbling around and him losing partners at the other end. Labuschange would have effectively been in the sheds had Jaiswal not shelled his sitter in the slips early in his innings. The situation improved when Marnus found reliable support in captain Pat Cummins, who approached the task with great responsibility. Their partnership proved crucial in bailing Australia out of a difficult position, combining to add 57 runs and extend their team's lead further.

Mohammad Siraj, showing notable improvement in his bowling, struck first in the match by removing Usman Khawaja, who had fought hard to survive until that point. Steve Smith and Marnus Labuschagne then showed resilience against India's threatening pace attack, gradually building Australia's lead. While Akash Deep bowled with commendable effort without success, it was Jasprit Bumrah who delivered the decisive blow with an exceptional spell, claiming three quick wickets that rattled Australia's middle order effectively reducing them from 80/2 to 91/6 with the lead still not out of India's reach.

Australia began with a lead in triple figures but the openers were constantly examined on their drives as the ball beat the edges on several occasions. It was not an easy time around for Sam Konstas and Usman Khawaja with Bumrah eventually getting the better of the former off a ripper. Khawaja and Labuschagne though rode on for some time but Bumrah continued to create chances from one end. Runs though came at a snail's pace as the ball was just doing enough to move both ways.

Well then, it just took around a couple of overs for India to wrap up the Australian innings, and it was that man Bumrah who did what was needed. But, in all fairness, the hosts hold all the aces in this match. They did tire out the Indian bowlers on the fourth day and this last-wicket stand between Lyon and Boland added pivotal 61 runs to the Aussie total, with Lyon scoring a brisk 41.

He then reckons that looking at the final wicket partnership of Australia, India might not have problems if they apply themselves well and bat sensibly.

We are just a few moments away from the fifth and final day to commence in this 4th Test at the MCG. The crowd is piling up gradually and the numbers could go well in excess of 50,000. It is currently bright and sunny out there in Melbourne. Australia will bat on as this is the word of mouth coming out from the camp.

Right then, 333 is the magical number that Australia currently lead by and they might have to force the issue early on the final day to avoid a draw. India though, no matter what, will have to put on a top batting performance to avoid defeat. We still have a long way to go, so, stick around as the action from Day 5 isn't far away.

On the other hand, India fought back hard with the ball and gave themselves a huge chance as Mohammed Siraj and especially Jasprit Bumrah did wonders to have the opposition 91/6 but they just didn't close things out and now, will have a very tricky job to do with the bat on Day 5 of the game to keep the BGT trophy in their grasp.

Australia batted for almost the whole chunk of Day 4 after having picked up the final Indian wicket and it was an innings filled with ups and down but eventually, this last wicket stand between Nathan Lyon and Scott Boland has proved to be telling. The lead is well over 300 and it will be interesting to see whether Australia declare right away or not.

Hello and a warm welcome to wherever you are you in the world. It is Day 5 of the Boxing Day Test between Australia and India and with all these results still possible, this match is heading towards the legendary status for so many reasons.
... DAY 5, SESSION ONE ...

The riveting day's play, marked by extraordinary displays of grit, valor, survival, and resistance from both teams, has perfectly set the stage for a thrilling final day finish in this Boxing Day Test. With India facing an uphill task, and Australia sniffing a victory, tomorrow promises to be a test of nerves, skill, and character. The historic ground has witnessed many memorable fifth-day finishes, as both teams prepare for one final push. Well then, 96 overs remain to be completed in the last three sessions to spare. India would be itching to get this last wicket super early in the day, while whatever runs come from the willows of Boland and Lyon, would potentially dash out India's chances. We are up for an EARLY START tomorrow as well as the first ball will be bowled at 4.30 am IST (11 pm GMT, the previous day) on Monday, 30th December. Till then, adios!

The pitch did show some signs of deterioration and the ball beat the edges innumerable times throughout the day, but it is still a decent one to bat on, given how the last-wicket stand for Australia stood up. Also, hard luck for Akash Deep who bowled his heart out but remained wicketless. India's fielding performance, however, fell below their usual standards, with Yashasvi Jaiswal's two dropped catches proving costly - opportunities that could have brought Australia's innings to an earlier close.

With 9 men down, Australia got more invaluable runs from the bat of Nathan Lyon and Scott Boland who resisted through the end of the day. Their determined stand not only frustrated and tired the Indian bowlers but also helped Australia surpass the psychologically important milestone of a 300-run lead, providing their team with additional insurance heading into the fifth and final day. Nathan Lyon did the most with the bat, but Scott Boland too showed good character for his 10 runs off 65 balls. Australia could have been effectively all out had Bumrah not overstepped in the final over when Lyon nicked into the slips, but that just sums up the day.

The pair's partnership lasted nearly 20 overs and yielded 57 valuable runs, providing Australia crucial breathing room. However, Mohammed Siraj broke through with a spectacular delivery to dismiss Labuschagne. By this point, Cummins had grown in confidence and continued to push Australia's advantage before his own dismissal, making his presence felt with important runs in the lower order. India shuffled its bowlers and even summoned spin in tandem, but the lower order did well enough.

Australia, despite being under considerable pressure entering into the third session, found stability through Marnus Labuschagne's resilient batting display. He found an ideal partner in Pat Cummins, who adopted a positive approach by rotating the strike and keeping the scoreboard moving rather than getting defensive under pressure. Cummins has become habitual of those pivotal contributions with the bat as he has done it numerous times, but the weightage this Test holds from an Australian perspective, that partnership for the seventh wicket could well prove to be the point of difference in this contest.

STUMPS, DAY 4 - SESSION SUMMARY - 33 Overs, 93 Runs, 3 Wickets - No reason to not love this format of cricket. From 91/6 to 228/9, Australia survives the day in a spectacular fashion. This Test match has been a pure box-office. To call it a remarkable display of cricket would be an understatement for what unfolded at the MCG on this Super Sunday! It was a test of pulse, grit, and character in the truest sense. As befitting this storied rivalry, the contest lived up to expectations, with neither side willing to concede ground. The spectators witnessed precisely what one would anticipate from these cricketing powerhouses, as momentum oscillated between the teams like a pendulum.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the post-Lunch session! The sun keeps shining over Melbourne as the two umpires walk out. Indian players also scatter out and take their fielding positions. The Aussie pairing of Marnus Labuschagne, unbeaten on 20, and Steven Smith on 2, will resume their stints with the bat. Akash Deep (9-2-20-0) to begin this second session of play with two slips and a gully in position. Off we go...
... DAY 4, SESSION 2 ...

Right then, while Australia holds the upper hand, this match is far from settled. India faces a dual challenge from here, as they need to put a lid on the scoring while also hunting wickets fast. Every run Australia adds makes their position more commanding, and time's ticking for India to turn this around. With Smith and Labuschagne, the two ever-dependable batters for Australia, the hosts will aim to extend this 158-run lead into a challenging one. With five more sessions left in this Test, the Aussies will surely try to bat throughout the day and dash the tourists out of the contest. Will India come back strong? Join us at 7.40 am IST (2.10 am GMT) for the post-Lunch session.

Usman Khawaja and Marnus Labuschagne didn't lose patience and tried to hang around for long. Bumrah was summoned back for the second spell and he continued to create chances consistently. In tandem, Siraj, who had an ordinary match, was dealt with a bit of ease, but looked much improved this time around and got the better of Usman Khawaja eventually off a ripper. But as the ball got a bit older, it certainly lost its bite and came onto the bat nicely. However, it kept beating the edges occasionally, but Smith and Labuschagne managed to see their side through the session.

In response, Australia's openers faced a torrid time against precise spells from Bumrah and Akash Deep as they bowled their hearts out. The new ball caused havoc, repeatedly beating the bat with late movement both ways. Bumrah struck first, producing a gem to remove Konstas. Meanwhile, Khawaja rode his luck after a dropped chance, never looking comfortable against the moving ball. The two pacers didn't give anything and the scoring rate remained at a snail's pace.

Play kicked off 30 minutes early to recover time lost to the previous day's rain interruption. The overnight pair of centurion Nitish Kumar Reddy and Mohammed Siraj returned to the crease with India still trailing by 116. Their resistance proved brief as Lyon outfoxed Nitish, helping Australia quickly clean up India's innings and secure a substantial 105-run lead.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! We all need a breather here! It has been an amazingly engaging first session of play with no side ready to back off one bit. Jasprit Bumrah and Akash Deep troubled the Aussie openers with Bumrah eventually getting the reward off a pearler against Konstas. The ball beat the outside edge on several occasions with Khawaja also getting an early lifeline off a dropped catch. But, with Bumrah out of attack now, this Aussie pair will aim to knock around and construct a good stand together as the hosts do have a decent lead at their helm. OUT! BOWLED'EM! Knocks him over through the defence! Bumrah gets the reward and provides the breakthrough for India! Jasprit Bumrah stays over the wickets and spears it on a fractionally fuller length, on off. It kisses the deck and just darts back into the batter off the surface, cutting the batter in half. Sam Konstas is forced on the front foot and goes for a defensive push but plays over the wrong line. The ball sneaks through the gap between the bat and the pad and rattles the top of the middle pole. A peach of a delivery from Bumrah to get rid of Sam Konstas and Australia lose their first wicket. 20/1 as Konstas departs on 8 (18).
